title: What makes it fast, exact and good to hold
intro_md: The headline work, as the repository and its docs record it.

cards.title: A PlayStation Portable core of its own
cards.lead_md: Written for Phobos in ares's style, from the PSP's documentation, tests and measurements taken on a real PSP. No code comes from other PSP emulators: PPSSPP was read only to learn how the PSP behaves.
points_md: No firmware needed: the PSP's system is emulated at a high level, from threads, files and timers to saves, sound, music, movies and the system's own dialogs.
The Allegrex CPU runs through a recompiler built on sljit, for ARM64 and x86-64, with an interpreter behind it.
Three renderers: an exact software renderer, Vulkan (accurate) and Vulkan (fast), at up to 10x the PSP's 480x272.
ISO, CSO, ZSO, DAX, JSO and CHD discs, read in place; save states that keep loading across builds.
cards.alt: God of War: Ghost of Sparta's main menu, drawn by Phobos at four times the PSP's resolution

link.label: The core's design, part by part

cards.title: Timed against a real PSP-1000
cards.lead_md: Since 19 October the PSP's graphics chip, the GE, takes about as long as the owner's PSP-1000 took over the same work (#269). Sony's peak rates, "Fast", stay as the opt-in.
points_md: Its costs are fitted to 3,373 display lists that PSP ran in four measurement rounds, with a median miss of 5.0% (#269); later rounds measured how the PSP's CPU slows the GE beside it (#279, #291).
It is checked against captures of real games' display lists from the same PSP. Since 21 October all eight judged game scenes are within 15% by their whole frame (#291).
Each change to the timing is run against all 266 games of the test library before it merges.

link.label: Parts 103 to 115 of the PSP core's notes

cards.title: The GE on a thread of its own
cards.lead_md: The PSP's graphics front end can run on a thread of its own, beside the emulated CPU, with exactly the results it gives inline.
points_md: In the core since 18 and 20 October (#272, #277). With it on, the frame is shown from the GE thread and the emulation thread's work is cut: Killzone from 149 to 74 million host instructions a frame.
Off by default. The app's "PSP Graphics Overlap" switch is built, and will be offered once On beats Off on the Retroid Pocket 6.
Next: an automatic handover between the two (see the roadmap).

cards.title: Nintendo 64, fast, on the stock driver too
cards.lead_md: ares's N64 core on parallel-RDP and Vulkan, with its recompilers tuned for ARM64.
points_md: CPU blocks link straight to each other and loops stay inside them: trips to the dispatcher fell from 10.1 to 0.6 million a second (#10).
The RSP's multiply-accumulates compile to inline NEON (#15, #16), and up to 256 parallel-RDP render contexts in flight took Mario Tennis's showcase from 82 late frames to 5 (#17).
Upscaling from 1x to 4x, the 64DD, Rumble and Controller Paks, and Turnip drivers from the app's GPU Driver Manager.
Since 21 October N64 games also draw on the Retroid Pocket 6's stock Qualcomm driver, which used to give a black picture (#292).

cards.title: Full speed on a handheld
cards.lead_md: Measured on a Retroid Pocket 6, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 handheld, as the work goes.
points_md: 18 of the 22 PSP games found slow averaged full speed at 1x in 150-second scripted runs with the 15 October nightly; v2.3.0 managed 7.
232 of the 266 PSP games averaged 59 fps or more at 5x internal resolution (2400x1360), in two-minute runs from launch that are mostly logos, intros and menus.
On 6 October the exact software renderer, drawing on several threads, took Peace Walker's title screen from 10.6 to 60 fps.
N64 games ran at a median 59.9 fps on the stock driver in all four games checked for #292.
cards.alt: F-Zero X racing on a Retroid Pocket 6 with Phobos's performance overlay reading 59.9 fps and its touch controls on screen

cards.title: Controller-first, and yours to theme
cards.lead_md: Made for handhelds: the D-pad and stick move a visible focus through every menu and the shoulder buttons switch tabs (#51). Touch controls are there too, with a layout for each system.
points_md: 37 themes, from Material You and Phobos's gold on deep space to One Dark, Dracula, Nord, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine and Synthwave '84, with glass, retrowave neon and an XMB-style backdrop.
A performance overlay, and controls remapped for one game, one console or all of them.
A screenshot pops into a film-strip card, hops into a folder, and says where it went (#273).
cards.alt: The Phobos Library on a Retroid Pocket 6: 34 systems as neon console tiles over a retrowave sun and grid, with a glass dock for Library, Console and Settings

cards.title: Always up to date
cards.lead_md: Settings → About updates the app straight from GitHub, from the tagged releases or from the nightly channel.
points_md: Every push to master publishes a nightly pre-release, in Modern and Legacy builds.
Tagged releases carry the desktop program as well: a Linux AppImage, a universal macOS app and a Windows Phobos.exe.
Every build is numbered from git history, the same on a laptop as on CI.
